answer: Pay agents through a weighted-score wager. Each round they stake tokens on forecasts that resolve later, such as silt at a river inlet, runoff from a mesa, or flood reach across a delta. Payout scales with stake times a proper score, so splitting one bankroll across a thousand identities earns exactly what a single identity would. Clones of one model also make the same forecast, so they add no information. Influence then follows capital at risk and accuracy, not account count, and creating more accounts gains nothing.
